As cyphr explained below, this change was pushed yesterday because "trusted users" with 100 comment contribution points were able to submit content without any restrictions.

Giving users a "trusted" status based on their comment karma was very naive from my side as cyphr demonstrated yesterday that such user could post thousands of posts in minutes.

There may be a trusted status later on without any restrictions, but for now, the throttling has to stay in place. Current limit is 1 post every 5 minutes (if you're lucky, you may get 2 posts in a row before the throttle kicks in).

This is not targeting people but it is affecting people. This is merely targeting spam bots. Without this throttle mechanism, bots can generate random titles and submission text and push thousands of gibberish posts in minutes destroying /v/all and pushing legitimate content tens of pages back. Maybe the limit could be lowered to 1 post per 3 minutes, but the throttle has to remain for now as I currently see no other easy way of dealing with this.
